text.tagline: Every keyboard in the building, catalogued.
text.blurb: Step inside a recording studio and meet its instruments: pianos, strings, brass, bells and more. Each sound comes with notes on how the real instrument works, and a Teacher's Guide brings it all into the classroom.
text.abstract: This Teacher's Guide accompanies the Studio Instruments Archive CD-ROM in the Discovery Shelf Series. It explains how each family of instruments makes its sound, and how the presets on the disc imitate them with nothing more than the sounds already on a school computer. Four lessons for grades 5 to 12 are included.
sections: Every instrument has something that vibrates: a string, a column of air, a bar of metal or wood. Did you know? The double siren in the picture on the cover was built in the nineteenth century to count vibrations, by blowing air through spinning disks with holes in them.
Students load three piano presets and describe the differences in attack and decay. Ask: why does a piano note fade, while an organ note does not?
Students compare a bowed string preset with a brass preset. Which one starts softly? Which one has a 'buzz'? Draw the loudness of each note over time.
Students strike bell and mallet presets and listen for the 'ring'. Discuss: why do bells sound out of tune when you play chords on them?
Using the DNA line shown in the Help file, students change one number in a preset and describe what changed. This is how sound designers work!
references: Bramblewood Learning Media, 'Discovering Sound', Discovery Shelf Series, 1994.

intro: Welcome to the Studio Instruments Archive, part of the Discovery Shelf Series from Bramblewood Learning Media.

In a recording studio there are many instruments: grand pianos, electric pianos, strings, brass, bells and more. This disc catalogues them for you, and lets you play each one with the Sound Recorder synthesizer on your own computer.
maker_note: Our Discovery Shelf titles are written with teachers, for students. Every sound on this disc was tested in real classrooms by the Bramblewood Teacher Panel.
We hope your students discover how much music hides inside a computer.
install: Insert the Studio Instruments Archive disc. In the Library tab, the disc appears as STUDARCH.
Open a folder (KEYS, STRINGS, BRASS ...) and double-click an instrument to play it.
Teachers: the Teacher's Guide is TEACHER.PDF; a short version is TEACHER.TXT.
license: You may use this disc on one computer at a time, at home or in one classroom. Lab packs and site licenses for schools are available: call 1-800-555-0171.
Teachers may copy the Teacher's Guide for their own students.

TEACHER.TXT: |Grade levels: 5 to 12.  Time: four lessons of 40 minutes.
Before class: check that the synthesizer opens and that the disc appears as STUDARCH in the Library tab. Headphones are recommended for lab use.
Lesson 1, the keyboard family. Lesson 2, strings and brass. Lesson 3, bells and mallets. Lesson 4, build your own sound. Full lesson plans and worksheets are in TEACHER.PDF.
Did you know? Each preset is one line of text called its DNA. Students can read it in the Help file and change one number at a time.
